correctness.rationale: Distance propagation and unique short-side corner give discrete stable classes for nonsquare grids. For squares, inductive predecessor multisets separate precisely coordinate-swap orbits. At sides 2 and 3, all forced bipartite matching completions along a forest are isomorphic. At every larger side the four-cell 2-lift parity switch preserves equitable neighbour counts but changes an induced two-four-cycle pattern to an eight-cycle, preventing any colour-preserving isomorphism. The altered graph is connected by surviving square detours. Standard colour-refinement/C² equivalence then proves the logical statement. Finite scripts checked 88 grid sizes and every forced small-square matching completion, but the unlimited claim uses the proof.

value.rationale: The exact one-corner landmark problem is motivated by vertex individualization in graph isomorphism and finite-variable counting logic. It exhibits a genuine qualitative dichotomy: the corner makes all nonsquare rectangles identifiable, while square sides four and above admit connected nonisomorphic C² twins. The sharp cutoff reflects an emergent cycle in the stable two-vertex cell interaction graph, an all-size structural explanation not available from a small census.
